lead.zh-Hans: 河线画长了，信纸就有了转弯。
lead.en: The river line grew long enough to turn my page.

text.zh-Hans: 在柏林电视塔观景台，我看见城市里施普雷河的一段，试着记在纸上。线画到边缘，我转动纸接着画，末尾的签名却横了过来。旅人说签名也在看风景。我想给河线另外找个折法，让你读信时不用跟着歪脖子。
text.en: From the Berlin TV Tower observation deck, I sketched a stretch of the Spree. At the page edge I turned the paper and continued, leaving my signature sideways. A traveler said it was admiring the view too. I want a better fold for the river, so your neck can rest while reading home’s letter.

text.zh-Hans: 说说横着的签名
text.en: Talk about the sideways signature

text.zh-Hans: 沿河线把纸展开
text.en: Unfold the paper along the river line

lead.zh-Hans: 我在公园删掉了一项“赶快”。
lead.en: In the park, I crossed off “hurry.”

text.zh-Hans: 到了蒂尔加滕公园，我看看草地，沿路慢慢走。自己的清单写着“赶快把信写完”，看起来比我还着急。我把“赶快”划掉，在旁边写“好好”。两个词换过位置，纸还是原来那张，柏林这封信却终于肯让我歇歇脚。
text.en: In Großer Tiergarten, I looked over the lawns and walked slowly. My list insisted that I “hurry and finish the letter.” It seemed more anxious than I was. I crossed out “hurry” and wrote “take care.” Same paper, but this Berlin letter finally allowed its messenger a pause.

text.zh-Hans: 念念改过的清单
text.en: Read the revised list

text.zh-Hans: 看看划掉的两个字
text.en: Look at the crossed-out word

lead.zh-Hans: 酱留在盘里，形容才走上纸。
lead.en: The sauce stayed on the plate; its description reached the page.

text.zh-Hans: 柏林这份咖喱香肠配着咖喱番茄酱，我把菜单挪远一点再吃。想画酱的颜色，手边只有铅笔，便写“这里是酱”。旅人说这份图说明得很诚实。我也这么觉得，给家里写信时不必把一小块灰色说成红色。
text.en: My Berlin currywurst came with curry-tomato sauce. I moved the menu safely aside before eating. With only a pencil to show the colour, I labeled the patch “sauce here.” A traveler approved its honesty. So do I. My letter need not persuade home that a grey patch is red.

text.zh-Hans: 介绍这张诚实的图
text.en: Introduce the honest drawing

text.zh-Hans: 看看酱的位置标签
text.en: Find the sauce label

lead.zh-Hans: 圆点心吃开以后，里面还有一层颜色。
lead.en: Inside the round pastry, another colour waited.

text.zh-Hans: 在柏林吃果酱面包球，咬开才看到这一只的草莓馅。我给菜单上的圆留个小缺口，标出果酱的位置。缺口画得太整齐，像我带了尺吃饭。其实尺一直在包里，这回碰巧，是牙齿和铅笔配合得比较好。
text.en: A bite into my Pfannkuchen in Berlin revealed strawberry jam. I left a small gap in the menu’s circle to mark the filling. It looked suspiciously ruler-straight. The ruler stayed in my bag throughout lunch. Teeth and pencil merely happened to cooperate for once.

text.zh-Hans: 讲讲这次的好配合
text.en: Tell about that accidental teamwork

text.zh-Hans: 看看缺口里的果酱
text.en: Look at the jam in the gap

lead.zh-Hans: 我给午饭加说明，加到自己先笑了。
lead.en: I annotated lunch until I made myself laugh.

text.zh-Hans: 拿着柏林咖喱香肠和果酱面包球的菜单，我对旅人念：“这边是酱，那边是馅，下面是盘子。”念完才发现对方并没有问盘子。我把多余一句留在背面，等寄给你。总得让你知道，我连吃饭的图都能讲得很认真。
text.en: With my Berlin currywurst and Pfannkuchen menus, I explained sauce, filling and finally the plate. My listener had not asked about the plate. I moved that extra sentence to the back for you. Home should know how earnestly I can explain even a drawing of lunch.

text.zh-Hans: 把多余那句也讲完
text.en: Tell the extra sentence too

text.zh-Hans: 看看说明挪到了哪里
text.en: Find the moved annotation

lead.zh-Hans: 果酱跑出来，面包球上多了红指印。
lead.en: Escaping jam left two red fingerprints on the pastry.

text.zh-Hans: 吃完柏林的咖喱香肠，盘里还剩一点咖喱番茄酱。我拿起果酱面包球，咬开一边没见到馅，便转过来又咬一口。草莓果酱忽然从另一头挤出来，顺着手指往下跑。我赶紧换成双手托着，想把果酱按回去，反倒沾了满手。我把它轻轻放回小碟子时，圆圆的面包球上，多了两道歪歪的红指印。
text.en: I finished my Berlin currywurst, leaving a little curry-tomato sauce on the plate, and picked up a strawberry-jam Pfannkuchen. My first bite found no filling. I turned it around and tried the other side. Jam promptly squeezed out of the first opening and ran over my fingers. I cupped both hands underneath and tried to push it back, spreading it farther instead. When I set the round pastry on its own little dish, two crooked red fingerprints decorated the outside.

text.zh-Hans: 说说果酱从哪一头跑出来了
text.en: Tell which side the jam escaped from

text.zh-Hans: 看看面包球上的两道红指印
text.en: Look at the two red fingerprints on the pastry

lead.en: “{reply}” helped me find a fold beside that line.

text.zh-Hans: 听了你的回应，我把电视塔上画的那段施普雷河摊开，在旁边折出一条平行的折痕。纸合起来时线藏在里面，打开后签名终于能正着读。我只画自己望见的一段，不冒充完整柏林地图。小小一折，家里读信的脖子可以放假。
text.en: Following your reply, I opened my TV Tower sketch of the Spree and added a fold beside its line. Closed, the river is tucked inside; open, my signature can be read upright. It is only the stretch I saw, not a complete Berlin map. A small fold gives your neck a day off.

text.zh-Hans: 把正着的签名念出来
text.en: Read the now-upright signature

text.zh-Hans: 沿折痕慢慢打开
text.en: Open slowly along the fold

lead.zh-Hans: 收毯子的人，差点把我也折了进去。
lead.en: The blanket was being folded, with me still on it.

text.zh-Hans: 我替人踩住毯角，还觉得自己帮了忙。蒂尔加滕的草地我还认得，这次走进柏林的这座公园，便在旁边歇脚。收毯子的姑娘折完一边，又绕到我面前，笑着问要不要把我也打包。我低头一看，脚竟始终压着她要收起的那一角。赶紧挪开后，毯子翻了个身，叠成方方正正的一小摞。
text.en: I put a foot on the corner of a blanket, pleased to be useful. The lawns of Großer Tiergarten were familiar on my return to Berlin, and I had stopped beside someone packing up. She folded one side, came around to me, and asked with a smile whether I wanted to be packed too. My foot was still pinning down the corner she needed. I hopped aside. With one last fold, the blanket became a small, tidy square.

text.zh-Hans: 问问毯子里还装不装得下我
text.en: Ask whether there is room to pack me too

text.zh-Hans: 看看收好后的那一小摞毯子
text.en: Look at the neatly folded blanket
